title: Change in arm mobility after self-application of yoga or cupping following unilateral breast cancer surgery
summary:
After breast surgery for breast cancer, many women have difficulty moving their arms. The shoulder often feels stiff, and scar tissue can also restrict mobility. This has a significant impact on everyday life. Yoga and cupping could help here—but before we investigate this in a large study, we first want to find out whether patients are able and willing to perform these exercises regularly at home.

We want to know: Are women able and willing to perform yoga exercises or cupping treatments independently at home after breast surgery? And do these exercises lead to positive changes in the mobility of the arm, shoulder, and scar?

Forty-five women who have limited mobility after unilateral breast surgery are participating in the study. They are randomly divided into three groups:

Yoga group: Participants learn special yoga exercises for the arm and shoulder and perform them independently at home.
Cupping group: Participants learn how to use cupping themselves to improve mobility.
Control group: This group does not perform any special exercises at first, but can participate in one of the programs free of charge after the study.

All participants will receive personal instruction before the study begins. During the study, we will measure the mobility of the arm and the scar, ask about limitations in everyday life, and record the participants' well-being. The participants will keep a diary of their exercises.
The study aims to show whether these self-treatments are feasible in everyday life and whether a larger follow-up study would be useful.

interventions.name: Cupping: 5 interventions (20 minutes each) within 1 week with a maximum of 1 day break over 3 weeks (15 interventions in total)
Yoga: 5 interventions (20 minutes each) within 1 week with a maximum of 1 day break over 3 weeks (15 interventions in total)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Cisgender women with a primary diagnosis of unilateral breast cancer (including DCIS)
• EGOG status 0 to 1 (determined by the study director, if necessary)
• Women who are proficient in German
• Signed declaration of consent
• Mental and intellectual capacity to perform the exercises
Exclusion criteria:
• Cisgender men
• Transgender individuals
• Pregnant women
• Women with recurrent breast cancer and women with an ECOG status of 2 or higher
• Use of blood thinners
